Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

Member: Quinn Grant
Requested Service: ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888
Date of Notice: 2026-08-02
Appeal Deadline: 2027-01-29

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29888 (arthroscopically aided anterior cruciate ligament repair/augmentation or reconstruction), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-02. The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree and ask that this determination be reversed based on the clinical record summarized below.

**1. The medical policy governing this request**

The notice states that the determination was made "under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria" but does not name or enclose that document. Based on my review, the UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange medical policy that lists CPT 29888 as an applicable code is titled "Surgery of the Knee." The version of that policy currently published by UnitedHealthcare is Policy Number 2026T0553JJ, with a stated effective date of September 10, 2026 — a date that falls after the date of this denial. I am therefore unable to confirm that this is the exact version and policy number applied to my case, and I formally request that UnitedHealthcare identify, by policy number and effective date, the specific version of "Surgery of the Knee" (or any other medical policy) applied to this determination, and provide me a complete copy of it, along with the specific clinical review criteria used to reach the denial, as required for a full and fair review.

The version of the policy I was able to obtain states, in its Coverage Rationale section:

"Surgery of the knee is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances. For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the: InterQual® CP: Procedures: o Arthroscopy or Arthroscopically Assisted Surgery, Knee..."

and separately, under Medical Records Documentation Used for Reviews:

"Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested; refer to the guidelines titled Medical Records Documentation Used for Reviews."

I was not able to obtain the text of the referenced InterQual® criteria themselves, as that document is a licensed, proprietary clinical tool not made available to members or the public. I am not quoting or attributing any specific conservative-treatment thresholds (such as required duration of therapy, number of visits, or medication trial length) to UnitedHealthcare, because I have not been given that text. I formally request that UnitedHealthcare provide the full text of the InterQual criteria (or whatever internal clinical criteria were actually applied) that it contends were not met, so that I may respond to the specific standard rather than a general description of it.

**2. The clinical record documents an adequate, and in fact extensive, trial of conservative treatment**

Notwithstanding the above request, the existing record already demonstrates a substantial conservative treatment trial that should satisfy any reasonable medical-necessity standard for ACL reconstruction:

- **Duration of symptoms:** 24 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest, indicating a chronic, non-resolving condition rather than an acute injury managed prematurely with surgery.
- **Supervised physical therapy:** 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing, from 2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21, comprising 20 completed visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection therapy:** A corticosteroid injection administered 2026-04-17, which provided only 3 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned.
- **Imaging confirming a structural lesion not amenable to further conservative care:** MRI of the knee on 2026-06-29 demonstrating a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with an associated bone bruise pattern, intact menisci, and no significant arthritis.
- **Functional instability despite completed conservative treatment:** The patient continues to experience recurrent instability with pivoting and has had the knee give way twice on stairs, despite completion of the physical therapy, bracing, medication, and injection trials above.
- **Exam findings:** Positive provocative ligamentous testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **No contraindications to surgery:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

Taken together, this record reflects: (a) a chronic, 24-month symptom course; (b) a completed, supervised, 10-week/20-visit physical therapy program with bracing; (c) a 6-month medication trial; (d) an injection trial; and (e) objective imaging confirming a complete ACL tear with ongoing mechanical instability despite all of the above. This is the clinical picture of a structural ligamentous injury that has already failed conservative management, not one for which further non-operative treatment is likely to be effective. The surgeon of record, Dr. Duval, has determined that ACL reconstruction is medically necessary based on this history, exam, and imaging.

**3. Requested action**

I ask that UnitedHealthcare:

1. Reverse the denial and approve CPT 29888 as requested by Dr. Duval; or
2. If UnitedHealthcare maintains that additional documentation is required, specify exactly what element of conservative treatment (e.g., additional duration, additional visits, additional modality) it contends is missing, with reference to the specific criteria document and section relied upon; and
3. Provide a copy of the full medical policy and any InterQual or other clinical criteria actually applied to this determination, including the applicable policy number and effective date in force on 2026-08-02.

I further request a peer-to-peer review between Dr. Duval and the medical director who reviewed this case, if that will assist in resolving this appeal.

**4. Preservation of further appeal rights**

This letter constitutes my first-level internal appeal, submitted within the 180-day window stated in the notice (deadline 2027-01-29). If this internal appeal is not resolved in my favor, I intend to pursue any further internal appeal level available under my plan, and thereafter an external review through the applicable Minnesota state process (the Minnesota Department of Commerce or Minnesota Department of Health, depending on how my plan is licensed), as provided under Minnesota law. Please advise of any additional internal appeal steps available before external review.

Enclosed with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21)
- Medication and injection records
- MRI report dated 2026-06-29
- Clinic/exam notes documenting instability and provocative testing
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Duval, orthopedic surgery
- [Any additional records the provider's office wishes to attach]

Please direct correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the contact information above, and copy [provider office contact name/fax/email], as my treating surgeon's office.

Thank you for your prompt reconsideration.

Sincerely,

Quinn Grant
